clue.text: Council disheartened by current measure for parking intervention

indicators.note: losing its heart, so the word council keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: the word council itself, before its inside goes
the amp is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: A local council stepping in to deal with parking problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current measure' reads as an electrical reading in a surface about traffic; a wheel clamp is the parking intervention.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel clamp is fitted to an illegally parked car, an enforcement step against bad parking.

clue.text: One appearing to race to embrace corporation up in suburbia?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is an old joke word for a paunch, not a company here; in a down clue 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The commuter belt is the ring of residential towns round a city from which workers travel in daily.

clue.text: Getting here requires a few flights — starts on awfully tense trip in chopper

definitions.text: Getting here requires a few flights

indicators.note: the starts of these five words give their first letters

explanation.surface: A nervous flyer facing several flights, including a scary helicopter trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flights' suggests air travel, but the definition means flights of stairs up to the top of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The loft room at the top of a house is reached by climbing several sets of stairs.

clue.text: Writing about cathedral beginning to tempt convert

indicators.note: the writing goes round the next pieces

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An author writing about a cathedral starting to lure someone to a new faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A proselyte is someone who has converted to a new religion or belief.

clue.text: American guy joining that chap in uninspiring opera

he refers to a man already mentioned

explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's La Boheme is one of the best-known operas in the repertoire.

clue.text: Thousand supporting America in the French location in Africa

parts.note: USA, United States of America
K is short for kilo, a thousand

explanation.surface: A thousand backing America in some French setting in Africa.

clue.text: Support doctor over operation in wider context

parts.note: to back someone is to support them

clue.text: Henry's first English Queen picked up something of a colourful character

explanation.walkthrough: Henry's first is H; ANNE read upwards is ENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish dye from a shrub, used to colour hair and skin.

clue.text: Steer badly, having awful consequences at the outset in fog

clue.text: Twisted neck is amongst items for discussion, linked to small difficulty in travelling

clue.text: Rather unusual oldish companies around University getting answer

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the university letter

explanation.definitionFit: This dated jocular British phrase is an emphatic yes, a play on I should say so, much like rather!

clue.text: Carrying on without a particular pattern?

definitions.text: Carrying on without a particular pattern?

parts.words: Carrying on without a particular pattern

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is one cryptic definition: the word means unrestrained, but split up it suggests something without a checked pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that continues without restraint goes on freely; read literally, the word means lacking checks, the squared design.

clue.text: Is written in a document in error

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript
taken as written

clue.text: Security I provided to Scottish town jurisdiction

clue.text: Untrue story I tell is curtailed, interrupted by sign of drunkenness

cut short, so the last letter goes

hic is the hiccup of a drunk

clue.text: Cheers enveloping half of them in passing

clue.text: Free to fail, securing nothing

clue.text: Seabird's cry in Aberdeen, repeated character to the fore

the letter that appears twice in the word

clue.text: Encouraging discovery, this cure I developed
